summary: A CAM Initiative reporter described a July 2026 demonstration in which three ChatGPT voice sessions on separate devices answered a shared conversational prompt independently, repeating or slightly varying one another rather than allocating a single synthetic turn. The linked TikTok video is identifiable, but the reviewing AI could not play it; no transcript or metadata preserves the exact speaker sequence, overlap or latency. OpenAI’s contemporary voice documentation describes full-duplex Live and separately warns that multi-speaker conversations are not yet optimised; it does not establish the specific modes or promise shared cross-device floor arbitration. The observed outcome is therefore a bounded first-person account of a local conversational collision, not proof of a platform-wide defect or a hidden orchestration component.

boundary_adjudication.decisive_blocker: The report preserves repeated independent replies but not intended speaker allocation, complete temporal sequence or whether parallel output was intentionally supported. Exact private networking or model orchestration is not required to establish observable coordination. Retain this bounded disposition unless material new evidence resolves those facts.

assessment_boundaries: The original video was not directly reviewed, so reported sequence, timing, overlap and exact device modes remain first-person evidence only.
Three separate sessions may not share a product-level cross-device arbitration feature; the class concerns the reported shared interaction floor, not a claimed internal implementation.
Provider documentation explicitly warns multi-speaker voice is not optimised; it cannot independently corroborate the demonstration.
No downstream high-stakes service, safety or personal harm is reported.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The CAM Initiative human reporter says three co-located ChatGPT voice sessions on separate devices produced repeated or similar replies rather than yielding to the preceding synthetic speaker. The TikTok short link identifies a primary audiovisual artefact, but direct playback failed for this review and no independent occurrence corroboration was located. Current OpenAI product documentation says Live can listen and speak simultaneously, while multiple speakers and overlapping audio can elicit unintended replies; its July launch post describes GPT-Live rollout, not the exact demonstrated configuration. The official statements bound expected voice behaviour but cannot verify this particular video. In the absence of playback, turn timing, intentional parallel output and routing remain unverified. The source-access gap itself impairs the detailed governance review without becoming the cause of the reported voice behaviour.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The reported repeated replies engage shared conversational-floor coordination. The outcome is Boundary because the intended turn allocation and complete sequence are not established. The first-person report of local interference remains evidence; lack of direct playback does not negate it. Provider documentation cannot establish this exchange’s modes or intended design. No missing private arbitration component or platform-wide defect is inferred. The separate S2 assessment of attributed local interference remains unchanged. Reviewer playback limits are not classified as the original occurrence’s evidence-access defect. No admitted external requirement is established.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case isolates a co-participant turn-allocation boundary and a separate evidence-access boundary. Its importance is bounded: repeated responses in a deliberate three-device voice test show a local coordination limitation, while unavailable primary timing evidence constrains confidence and warrants provenance-preserving recovery.
